subject: tiger keelback snake
title: This Snake Steals Poison From Toads and Stores It in Its Neck

scenes.text: This snake is poisonous. But it can't make poison.
Japan's tiger keelback has glands on the back of its neck, filled with a toxin that attacks the heart.
The toxin isn't the snake's own. It comes from the toads it eats.
On one Japanese island with no toads, the snakes have none. Feed them toads, and the poison appears.
Snakes that carry it arch their necks toward an attacker. Snakes without it are more likely to flee.
And a mother with a full supply passes it to her young. They hatch already armed.

description:
The tiger keelback snake of Japan gets its defensive poison from the toads it eats.
It stores toad toxins called bufadienolides in glands on the back of its neck. Snakes on the toad-free island of Kinkazan have none, but gain it when fed toads in the lab. Armed snakes arch their necks toward a predator; unarmed ones tend to flee. Mothers with high levels pass the toxin on to their offspring. The study appeared in PNAS in 2007.
Which animal has the smartest borrowed weapon?
first_comment: Hatchlings from a toad-free island gained the toxin in the lab once they were fed toads. Which animal has the best stolen weapon?
